overview: 72 official Qs (2008: 3, 2012: 5, 2017: 15, 2019: 37, 2025: 12). Mostly one-liners (34 with options, 27 stem-only), with 2025 adding matching (3), chronology, A-R and statement Qs. Kakatiya/Reddi/Vijayanagara kings and Telugu author→work pairs carry the weight; 2 Qs were deleted and 2 accepted multiple keys.

possibility.angle: Major dynasties: Kakatiyas (origin, capitals, kings, titles, inscriptions, fall)
possibility.evidence: part of 20 Qs on major dynasties (2012×2, 2017×7, 2019×7, 2025×4)
possibility.what_they_ask: First inscription to name them, overlords, who shifted capital, title → ruler, inscription → ruler (matching), who defeated/captured whom and when

possibility.angle: Major dynasties: Reddis and Vijayanagara (titles, taxes, order, campaigns, administration, foreign accounts)
possibility.evidence: same 20-Q leaf: Reddi title (2017), Puriti Pannu (2019), Reddi order (2025), Potnuru pillar (2025), Kandachara (2019), Paes/Sewell (2012, 2017)
possibility.what_they_ask: Which Reddi king had a title/tax, chronological order, where Krishnadevaraya set his pillar, which traveller described what, department → function

possibility.angle: Minor dynasties: Velanati/Nellore Chodas, Chalukya-Chola viceroys, Musunuris, Recherlas, Palnadu
possibility.what_they_ask: Capital of a dynasty, lake/place named in an inscription, liberation-movement leader, Palnadu battle site, viceroy titles, A-R on Nellore Chodas

possibility.angle: Socio-religious conditions (castes, sects, festivals, sati, law)
possibility.what_they_ask: Meaning of a social term (Vipravinodins, samayamu), festival of a dynasty, which traveller saw sati, which law book holds a tenet, seat of a deity

possibility.angle: Economic conditions (guilds, ports, salt, tanks, trade texts)
possibility.what_they_ask: Guild → occupation, port's other name, product of a place, tank → builder, inscription with tank rules, text with trade data, number of ports

possibility.angle: Growth of Telugu language and literature (poet → work, language, women poets, music)
possibility.what_they_ask: Author of a named work, which work is NOT by a poet, language of a royal composition, title of a poet, matching author–work lists

possibility.angle: Art and architecture (Hampi, Lepakshi, Tadipatri, Kakatiya temples, music, folk arts)
possibility.what_they_ask: Monument → place, popular name of a temple, style features, source text of sculptures, instrument/inscription, rural entertainment form

traps.trap: Same-circle author swap in author–work lists
traps.spot: Matching codes or 'wrong match' with poets of one court [Tikkana circle, Reddi court, Vijayanagara women poets]
traps.fix: Ketana – Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam; Marana – Markandeya Puranam; Tikkana – Nirvachanottara Ramayanam; Manchena – Keyurabahu Charitra
traps.pyq: 'Ketana – Markandeya Puranam' → Ketana wrote Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam [mains-2025-paper1#14]; 'Gangadevi – Marichi Parinayam' → wrong, Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam [mains-2025-paper1#18]

traps.trap: Subject of the work offered as its author
traps.spot: A name in the title of the work appears among the options
traps.fix: Varadambika Parinayam is about Varadamba, written by Tirumalamba
traps.pyq: 'Who wrote Varadambika Parinayam' → Tirumalamba, not Varadamba [mains-2017-paper2#34]

traps.trap: Builder vs mover of the capital
traps.spot: Options are successive kings of one dynasty and the stem says 'shifted'
traps.fix: Rudradeva began Orugallu; Ganapatideva shifted the capital from Anumakonda
traps.pyq: 'shifted the capital from Anumakonda to Warangal' → Ganapatideva [group2-2012-paper1#102]

traps.trap: Language of a royal/sastra work given as Telugu
traps.spot: Telugu-era author but the question asks 'in which language'
traps.fix: Nritta Ratnavali (Jayapa) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Krishnadevaraya) are Sanskrit; Amuktamalyada is Telugu
traps.pyq: 'Nritta Ratnavali was composed by Jayapa in' → Sanskrit [group2-2012-paper1#103]

traps.trap: Traveller swap (Paes, Nuniz, Abdur Razzaq, Conti)
traps.spot: Foreign visitors listed together with a 'who described' stem
traps.fix: Paes = Krishnadevaraya's looks and House of Victory; Nuniz = chronicle; Abdur Razzaq = 300 ports (Devaraya II)
traps.pyq: 'described the physical features of Krishnadevaraya' → Paes, not Nuniz [group2-2012-paper1#133]

traps.trap: Conquest site offered instead of the pillar site
traps.spot: Options list forts of the same campaign
traps.fix: Udayagiri, Kondaveedu were captured; the victory pillar is at Potnuru

traps.trap: Overlord mixed with a same-name dynasty
traps.spot: Badami Chalukyas and Eastern Chalukyas listed beside Rashtrakutas
traps.fix: Kakatiyas: Rashtrakuta feudatories first, later Kalyani (not Badami) Chalukyas

traps.trap: Wrong person given the zenith in an A-R
traps.spot: Reason claims a dynasty peaked under a king who needed outside help
traps.fix: Nellore Chodas peaked under Tikka I; Manumasiddhi II was restored by Ganapatideva
traps.pyq: 'Nellore Chodas at zenith under Manumasiddhi II' → false [mains-2025-paper1#16]

traps.spot: Deity seat or capital asked with one of these names
traps.fix: Vasavi's seat = Penugonda (West Godavari); Penukonda (Anantapur) = later Vijayanagara capital
traps.pyq: 'main seat of the goddess Vasavi' → Penugonda [mains-2019-paper2#18]

techniques.name: Two-pair lock for matching codes
techniques.how: Find the two pairs you are surest of [usually the most famous poet or inscription]; keep only codes containing both; check one more pair if two codes remain.
techniques.example: Tikkana – Nirvachanottara (c-II) and Ketana – Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam (a-III) → only 'a-III, b-I, c-II, d-IV' [mains-2025-paper1#14]; Bayyaram – Mailamba and Motupalli – Ganapatideva → 'a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II' [mains-2025-paper1#21]

techniques.name: Ends-first chronology
techniques.how: Fix the first and last ruler of the series, then check only those positions in the options.
techniques.example: Reddis: Anavota before Anavema, Pedakomati Vema last → 'C, B, A, D' [mains-2025-paper1#19]

techniques.name: Court-circle grouping for 'not written by'
techniques.how: List the poet's known works; the odd one usually belongs to a court colleague writing in another language.
techniques.example: Srinatha: Haravilasam, Sivaratri Mahatmyam, Palnati Veera Charitra; Madanavilasabanam is Vamana Bhatta Bana's Sanskrit work → that option [mains-2025-paper1#23]

techniques.name: Period filter for culture options
techniques.how: Drop art/entertainment forms that took shape centuries later before choosing.
techniques.example: Harikatha, modern drama, Burrakatha are 19th–20th c. → Bommalata with Yakshagana [prelims-2019#87]

techniques.name: Verb anchoring
techniques.how: Read the verb: began/built, shifted, introduced, described, translated – then pick the king or author tied to that exact act.
techniques.example: 'translated into Telugu the Ganitasarasangraha' → Pavuluri Mallana; Nannaya and Narayana Bhatta are Mahabharata names [prelims-2019#74]

confusions.remember: Paes = what he saw (king, city, House of Victory); Nuniz = history of the dynasty
Rudradeva = independence, Anumakonda inscription; Ganapatideva = shift to Orugallu, Motupalli charter
Rudrama's title from victory over Devagiri Yadavas; Prola I built Kesari Samudram
Gangadevi = Madhura Vijayam; Tirumalamba = Varadambika Parinayam; Mohanangi = Marichi Parinayam
Ketana = Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, Vijnaneswaramu, title Abhinava Dandi; Marana = Markandeya Puranam; Manchena = Keyurabahu Charitra
Srinatha = Haravilasam, Palnati Veera Charitra; Vallabharaya = Kreedabhiramam; Bana = Madanavilasabanam
Prolaya Nayaka = Musunuri liberation leader; Prolaya Vema = first Reddi king, Rachuru Durga Vibhala
Racha Vema = Puriti Pannu tax, last Kondavidu king; Kumaragiri = Vasantotsavam patron
Vitthala = stone chariot; Hazara Rama = Ramachandra temple, royal chapel
Lepakshi = huge Nandi + murals; Tadipatri = gopuras that excel Hampi's Vitthala
Chitrameli = agriculturists' guild; Nakaramu = merchants; Samayamu = Kakatiya caste association
Annamacharya = sankirtanas/padas; APPSC keyed Tyagaraja as pioneer of the kriti

anchors: Magallu inscription = first mention of Kakatiyas; Kazipet = Beta I; Bayyaram = Mailamba
Anumakonda inscription = Rudradeva; Motupalli abhaya charter = Ganapatideva; Motupalli = Desiyakkonda Pattanam
1263 Muttukur: Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva; 1323: Prataparudra captured by Ulugh Khan
Raichur Doab = between Krishna and Tungabhadra
Reddi order: Prolaya Vema → Anavota → Anavema → Kumaragiri → Pedakomati Vema (Sangeeta Chintamani)
Jayapa (Gaja-sahini of Ganapatideva) – Nritta Ratnavali in Sanskrit; basis for Ramappa dance sculptures
Pavuluri Mallana – Ganitasara Sangraham (Telugu rendering of Mahaviracharya)
Errana – Narasimha Puranam; Appayacharya – Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayam
Thousand Pillar temple = trikuta: Rudreswara, Vasudeva, Surya
Robert Sewell – A Forgotten Empire; Abdur Razzaq – 300 ports
Porumamilla inscription = 12 rules for tank building; Surambika – Santana Sagaram
checklist: Which dynasty and century? Kakatiya (12–14th), Reddi (14–15th), Vijayanagara (14–16th) – drop out-of-period options.
What act does the verb ask: built, shifted, introduced, described, wrote, translated?
Is a name in the work's title being passed off as its author?
For 'in which language', separate Sanskrit sastra/royal plays from Telugu kavyas.
Matching: lock two sure pairs before reading all codes.
Watch near-twin names: Penugonda/Penukonda, Prolaya Nayaka/Prolaya Vema, Rayagaja/Arigaja Kesari.
